header: Scanned pages are tilted by a fraction of a degree (up to 0.4 degrees on the roster pages): a long vertical rule drifts ~25 px across the page, which breaks any straight-line search and puts a row's text at a different height from the ruled line beside it. So I straighten every page first. The tilt is MEASURED from the page itself: the angle at which the long rules (vertical) line up best.

members.name: k
doc: horizontal drift per vertical pixel of a vertical rule (dx/dy); 0 = perfectly upright

members.name: strength
doc: how dark the best vertical path is, as a share of the page height (a low value = no rules to measure from)

symbols.name: score
symbols.sig: function score(g: Gray, k: number, step: number): { sharp: number; peak: number }
doc: I score a candidate tilt this way: the sharper the column profile along tilted vertical paths, the better the rules line up.

symbols.name: estimateTilt
symbols.sig: export function estimateTilt(g: Gray, maxTilt = 0.02): Tilt
doc: Measures the tilt of a page from its vertical rules: a coarse search first, then a finer one around the best.

symbols.name: deskewPng
symbols.sig: export async function deskewPng(png: Buffer, k: number): Promise<{ png: Buffer; angleDeg: number }>
doc: Rotates the picture so that the rules become vertical/horizontal. Returns the straightened PNG and the angle used (degrees, clockwise).
